measurements.source_table: Abstract (Results/tolerability sentence: "Two subjects experienced rash, one a reversible platelet decrease, and mild injection site tenderness was noted.")
measurements.notes: HUMAN clinical row — the priority class for this dataset. One subject in the Phase I programme had a platelet decrease explicitly described as reversible. GRADING RATIONALE (non-obvious, please read): the abstract gives NO platelet count, no nadir, no percent decline, no denominator and no route/dose attribution, so the grade rests only on the qualitative descriptors available. Grade 1 is assigned because the event is stated to be reversible, no intervention, dose interruption, dose reduction, bleeding or discontinuation is described, and the paper's own conclusion is that the drug was "generally well tolerated intravenously and subcutaneously". Grade 1 should be treated as a FLOOR, not a confirmed ceiling: if the full text (inaccessible - see extraction_notes) shows a count in the 50-99 x10^9/L band or a dose interruption, this row becomes grade 2, and grade 3 if <50 x10^9/L or antibody-mediated. dose_or_conc_value/unit are TBD rather than the printed 0.1-6 mg/kg i.v. band because the abstract does not say whether the affected subject was in the i.v. escalation or an s.c. cohort - assigning the band would be an invented attribution. readout_unit is n_subjects rather than pct_incidence because the abstract states no total N, so an incidence percentage cannot be computed without fabrication. EXCLUSION LINE: ISIS 104838 targets TNF-alpha mRNA and has no intended antiplatelet or antithrombotic pharmacology, so this platelet decrease is an UNINTENDED effect and is correctly in scope; none of the on-target-antithrombotic exclusion (ARC1779 / pegnivacogin class) applies here.

The grade-0 label here means 'no platelet event observed/reported at this exposure', NOT 'no coagulation effect'; the aPTT effect is real, transient, dose-ordered and explicitly labelled a PS class effect. UNIT AMBIGUITY, FLAGGED NOT RESOLVED: the sentence reads as the magnitude of prolongation in seconds (i.e. +18 s over baseline). It could conceivably be an absolute post-infusion PTT value, but 18 s would sit below a normal aPTT reference range (~25-35 s), which makes the increment reading far more likely. Recorded exactly as printed rather than converted or re-based. effect_vs_control is TBD because this was a single-arm dose-ranging trial with no placebo group and the abstract gives no baseline PTT.

measurements.source_table: Abstract (Results)
measurements.notes: EXPLICIT NEGATIVE, GRADE 0. Locus sentence: 'There were no corresponding alterations in hematology parameters including RBC or platelet counts.' Young adult cynomolgus monkeys, slow IV bolus every other day for 28 days (14 doses), dose levels 0, 2, 10 and 50 mg/kg/injection; basic group 3M+3F sacrificed 2 days after the last dose. Grade 0 per the rubric's 'no platelet signal at tested exposure'. readout_value=TBD because the abstract prints NO numeric platelet counts and the full text is paywalled — the finding is qualitative-only at this locus; a number here would be fabricated. The abstract makes a single blanket hematology statement covering the whole study rather than a per-dose breakdown, so this row and the 10 and 50 mg/kg rows all derive from that one sentence; they are split by dose group because the study genuinely ran three treated dose levels and the negative applies to each, but they are NOT three independent observations. The abstract's closing sentence independently corroborates this dose: '2 mg/kg ISIS 2302 produced no remarkable alterations.' Vehicle-control (0 mg/kg) row not emitted — no control platelet value is printed.

measurements.source_table: Abstract (Results)
measurements.notes: EXPLICIT NEGATIVE, GRADE 0. Same locus sentence as the 2 mg/kg row: 'There were no corresponding alterations in hematology parameters including RBC or platelet counts.' 10 mg/kg/injection IV every other day x 14 doses over 28 days. Notable because this dose DID produce other treatment-related toxicity in the same animals (periocular swelling on day 1, one markedly lethargic monkey after the first dose, renal proximal tubular eosinophilic granules and vacuolation, dose-dependent clotting-time prolongation) — the platelet compartment was nonetheless unaffected, which is what makes this a useful negative rather than an uninformative one. readout_value=TBD: no numeric platelet count is printed in the abstract and the full text is paywalled.

measurements.source_table: Abstract (Results)
measurements.notes: EXPLICIT NEGATIVE AT THE TOP DOSE, GRADE 0 — the most informative row in this source. Same locus sentence: 'There were no corresponding alterations in hematology parameters including RBC or platelet counts.' 50 mg/kg/injection by slow IV bolus every other day for 28 days (14 doses) is a very high first-generation full-PS exposure, and it produced renal tubular changes and free RBC in proximal tubular lumens in the same animals yet left platelet counts unaltered. This anchors the monkey side of any human-to-animal extrapolation for PS-ASO platelet safety: NHP platelet counts were insensitive to 4 weeks of high-dose uniform PS-DNA. This dose group also included 2 monkeys/sex held for a 28-day treatment-free recovery period. readout_value=TBD: the abstract prints no numeric platelet count and the full text is paywalled (Elsevier, Unpaywall oa_status=closed), so no value could be seen.

measurements.source_table: Abstract (Results)
measurements.notes: BLEEDING GRADED ON ATTRIBUTION, NOT ON THE KEYWORD — this row exists specifically so a keyword-driven reader does not mistake it for a grade-3 haemorrhagic event. Locus sentences: 'Other clinical observations included ... bruising in all dose groups throughout the study. Bruising was associated with a dose-dependent prolongation of clotting times, particularly activated partial thromboplastin times (APTT), that was transient in nature. Bruises occurred around site of intravenous dosing or blood collection, and were manifested as subcutaneous hemorrhages upon microscopic evaluation. There were no corresponding alterations in hematology parameters including RBC or platelet counts.' The authors therefore attribute the haemorrhage to a coagulation-cascade effect (aPTT prolongation, the well-known intrinsic-pathway effect of polyanionic PS oligonucleotides) and EXPLICITLY exclude a platelet-count cause in the very next clause. Per the rubric, grade 3 requires a haemorrhagic event ATTRIBUTABLE TO THROMBOCYTOPENIA; attribution here is explicitly to coagulopathy with normal platelets, so the thrombocytopenia grade is 0. is_platelet_specific=FALSE: adjacent-haematology fallback row, retained because the bleeding/no-thrombocytopenia dissociation is itself evidence for this endpoint. Dose recorded as the band 2-50 because the abstract says 'all dose groups' without a per-dose incidence; whether the 0 mg/kg vehicle group is included in 'all dose groups' is NOT resolvable from the abstract, and the localisation of bruises to IV dosing and blood-collection sites means a procedure-related component cannot be excluded. readout_value=TBD: no incidence, count or severity figure is printed.

measurements.source_table: Abstract (Results and Conclusion)
measurements.notes: ADJACENT-HAEMATOLOGY ROW, is_platelet_specific=FALSE. Included only because it is the mechanism the authors assign to the bruising row above, so without it that row's grade-0 attribution is unsupported; it is not an attempt to widen scope beyond the platelet endpoint. Loci: 'Bruising was associated with a dose-dependent prolongation of clotting times, particularly activated partial thromboplastin times (APTT), that was transient in nature' (Results) and 'In general, 10 and 50 mg/kg ISIS 2302 produced dose-dependent changes in clotting times and the kidney that were reversible, while 2 mg/kg ISIS 2302 produced no remarkable alterations' (Conclusion). Dose recorded as the band 10-50 exactly as the conclusion delimits it; 2 mg/kg is stated to have produced no remarkable alterations, so the coagulation effect has an apparent threshold above 2 mg/kg. thrombocytopenia_grade=0 because this readout involves no platelet compartment at all — the grade column reflects the thrombocytopenia endpoint, and the same animals had unaltered platelet counts. readout_value=TBD: the abstract prints no aPTT seconds, no fold-change and no timepoint. Effect described as transient and, in the overall conclusion, reversible.

measurements.source_table: Abstract (Results)
measurements.notes: IN-VITRO MECHANISM ROW — cell-free binding competition, NOT a platelet assay; grade 0 is a schema floor, not an observed platelet null. species=NA because the abstract does NOT state the species of the Factor H used; it was NOT assumed to be human, which matters because a human-source in-vitro row would otherwise be miscounted toward this lane's human-data priority. No concentrations, IC50 or elution percentages appear in the abstract, hence dose and readout_value TBD. Mechanistically this is polyanion competition for the heparin-binding site of Factor H — the same physicochemical PS-polyanion property invoked for platelet-protein binding, which is why the row is worth carrying despite not being platelet-specific.

oligos.notes: CHEMISTRY, as printed: PMID 19012510 abstract — "a 2'-methoxyethyl modified phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide that is complementary to clusterin mRNA"; PMID 18245546 title — "a 2'-methoxyethyl phosphorothioate antisense to clusterin". backbone_chemistry=full_PS is taken from those explicit "phosphorothioate" statements; ps_count left TBD because no fetched source prints a linkage count (a fully-PS 21-mer would have 20 linkages, but this was NOT asserted by any source and is therefore not recorded). gapmer_design=TBD: no fetched source states the wing/gap/wing arrangement. oligo_class=ASO_gapmer is the class assignment for a second-generation 2'-MOE PS ASO acting by RNase H-mediated knockdown of CLU mRNA (sources describe it as inhibiting/reducing clusterin production, not splice-switching); the gapmer motif itself is unverified, hence gapmer_design=TBD rather than a guessed motif. PURITY: deliberately NOT recorded. The only purity figure I found in any fetched text ("length purity of >95% with a phosphodiester content of <0.3%") appears in PMC3388571 (PMID 22588555, Br J Cancer 2012;106:1945-52), which now carries a 2025 Editorial Expression of Concern (PMID 39627565, Br J Cancer 2025;132:138). I excluded that paper from design_source and did not carry its purity value forward. That same paper also printed the identical sequence, so the sequence is safe — it rests on the three uncompromised sources listed in design_source. DOSE CONTEXT for the measurement rows: the biologically effective / phase 2-3 dose is 640 mg IV over 2 h (PMID 16145049 abstract: "The optimal biologic dose for OGX-011 at the schedule used is 640 mg"). max_phase=phase_3_discontinued: two phase 3 trials reported final negative analyses — SYNERGY (PMID 28283282) and AFFINITY (PMID 29033099).

Verbatim: "In the first Phase I study of custirsen in prostate cancer, no dose-limiting toxicities were reported at the doses of custirsen investigated (up to 640 mg); all toxicities were grade 1/2 and typically occurred within the first week of administration. For patients receiving the 640 mg dose, the most frequent adverse events included thrombocytopenia, anemia, and leukopenia". GRADE 1 rationale: the source explicitly caps ALL toxicities at CTCAE grade 1/2 and reports no DLTs and no intervention, which is the rubric's mild/reversible band. readout_value=TBD because the source names thrombocytopenia as a most-frequent AE but prints no incidence figure — not estimated. WHY THIS ROW MATTERS: NCT00054106 (verified on ClinicalTrials.gov) is 'A Phase I Study Of Combination Neoadjuvant Hormone Therapy And Weekly OGX-011 Prior To Radical Prostatectomy', interventions buserelin + flutamide + custirsen sodium + surgery. There is NO cytotoxic chemotherapy, so unlike every other custirsen clinical row below, this thrombocytopenia signal is not confounded by a myelosuppressive backbone. Corroborated by the primary paper's own abstract (PMID 16145049): "Only grade 1 and 2 toxicities were observed" across 40-640 mg in n=25. I could not obtain the JNCI full text (Unpaywall oa_status=closed) so the per-dose toxicity table was not read.

measurements.notes: THE ONLY CONTROLLED CUSTIRSEN PLATELET ESTIMATE I could obtain, and the strongest causal-attribution row here. Meta-analysis of 3 randomized controlled trials, 1709 patients (857 custirsen + docetaxel-or-cabazitaxel + prednisone vs 852 chemotherapy + prednisone alone). Because both arms receive the same myelosuppressive taxane backbone, the odds ratio isolates the custirsen increment: adding custirsen multiplies the odds of thrombocytopenia 2.62-fold. Verbatim: "thrombocytopenia (OR = 2.62, 95% CI = 1.82-3.77, P < .001)". GRADE 2 rationale: a named thrombocytopenia adverse event, significantly more frequent on custirsen and reported by the authors as a treatment-related complication requiring clinical attention, places it above the mild band; the source prints NO CTCAE severity band and no platelet counts, so grade 3 is not supportable and was not assigned. This is a grading judgement on an unstated severity, flagged accordingly. Licence is CC-BY-NC-ND (read from the article's own licence field), i.e. NOT CC-BY, hence summary_stat rather than cc_by.

It is included because anti-drug immunogenicity is the mechanistic axis of the rubric's grade-3 'immune-mediated thrombocytopenia with confirmed anti-platelet antibodies' band, and this is the paper's own direct measurement of it in the compound under study. Table 3 values: 6068 study samples screened; 65 potentially positive samples; 35 patients with at least 1 positive time point at SCREENING; 1 patient with at least 1 CONFIRMED positive time point; 2 samples confirmed positive; titer 50 (1:50). measurements.notes: COHORT 1 = danvatirsen 200 mg MONOTHERAPY, n=5 Japanese patients with advanced solid malignancies, NCT03394144. This is the cleanest danvatirsen monotherapy platelet signal available: platelet count decreased was the SINGLE most common adverse event, causally related to danvatirsen, in 60% of patients. Graded 1 (not higher) because Table 2 records ZERO grade >=3 platelet events in cohort 1 and no dose reductions were required in cohort 1 - so all three events were CTCAE grade 1-2 with no intervention. That is categorically different from the anti-vWF (ARC1779) and anti-FIXa (pegnivacogin) aptamers excluded by the brief, whose whole purpose is to inhibit platelet function. measurements.source_table: Results 3.4 'Platelet Aggregation Analysis' (Methods 2.5)
measurements.notes: HUMAN EX-VIVO PLATELET FUNCTION under a marketed 2'-MOE PS ASO - the row type NCATS asked for. Agonist ADP 1.8 uM; Born turbidimetric aggregometry on platelet-rich plasma, CHRONO-LOG 700 aggregometer, at week 36 of volanesorsen. Prespecified normality criterion (Methods 2.5): >=50% light transmission within 3 min indicates NO impairment of aggregation; 62% clears it. n=4 patients vs 4 matched healthy controls, no significant difference. Graded 0. Interpretive value: volanesorsen lowers the platelet COUNT by ~34% without impairing the FUNCTION of the platelets that remain - so count and function dissociate, and an in-vitro activation/aggregation assay is not a surrogate for the count endpoint.
